case_name: Cherlopalli Cheliminabi Saheb & Anr. v State of A.P.
respondent:
State of A.P.
Supreme Court of India

31 January 2003
Appeal (Crl.) 260 of 19961
The Judgment was delivered by : N. Santosh Hegde, J.
1.  The appellants were accused Nos.1 and 3 before the II Additional Sessions Judge, Chittoor at Madanapalle in S.C.No.53/92. They were charged for an offence punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC before the Additional Sessions Judge who found them guilty and convicted them for an offence punishable under Section 304 Part II and sentenced both the accused to undergo R.I. for a period of 4 years. The said conviction and sentence has been upheld in appeal by a Single Judge of the High Court of Judicature, A.P. at Hyderabad in Criminal Appeal No.1272/92.

facts: The appellants were accused Nos.1 and 3 before the II Additional Sessions Judge, Chittoor at Madanapalle in S.C.No.53/92.
On 25.5.1991 at about 8 p.m., there was an altercation between the wife of the Ist appellant herein and the wife of the deceased in regard to taking water from the tap.

The prosecution before the trial court examined 12 witnesses out of whom PW-1 was the wife of the deceased, PW-2 was the son of the deceased, PWs. 3 to 6 were neighbours who allegedly witnessed the incident while PWs. 7 and 8 were panch witnesses for the recovery of the weapon.
The trial court rejected the second dying declaration Ex.P-13 on the ground that the same was dated subsequent to the death of the deceased, therefore, it was not safe to rely upon the same.
It is stated that as per the advise of doctor, PW-9, the deceased was shifted to Tirupati hospital where another statement of the deceased was recorded by PW-11 which is marked as Ex.P-13.
issues: Whether the dying declaration Ex.P-4 can be relied upon for basing a conviction?
Whether the prosecution has explained how the accused persons suffered injuries and by whom?
Whether the prosecution version of the incident becomes doubtful in the absence of any explanation from the prosecution as to the injuries on the appellant?
petitioner_arguments: Ex.P-4 is not a document on which any court can safely place reliance.
It is highly doubtful whether really the statement of this nature was ever recorded by PW-11 during the life time of the deceased.
The prosecution has recovered only one weapon, therefore, it is difficult to appreciate the prosecution case how by one single weapon all these four accused persons could have stabbed the deceased.
There is an obligation on the part of the prosecution to explain the injuries suffered by the accused.
respondent_arguments: There is no reason to doubt the evidence of PW-11, the investigating officer, because no suggestion of any sort has been made to this witness as to his impartiality.

This witness PW-11 had no reason to depose or to falsely implicate these appellants because the case was not even being investigated by him, ultimately therefore, the result of the case would be of no consequence to this witness.
court_reasoning: The prosecution version of the incident becomes doubtful in the absence of any explanation from the prosecution as to the injuries on the appellant.

All these suspicious circumstances surrounding Ex.P-4, coupled with the fact that the close relatives of the deceased have not supported the prosecution case and the absence of explanation from the prosecution as to the injuries on the accused gives rise to a serious doubt as to the correctness of Ex.P-4 which, in our opinion, cannot be relied for the purpose of basing a conviction.
holding: The appeal has to succeed; hence, we set aside the judgment and conviction of the courts below and allow this appeal.
The appellants shall be released forthwith, if not required in any other case.
